s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin condition with erythematous papules and lymphoid infiltrate
salient_findings: Erythematous papules with crusts and excoriations on the trunk and upper extremities
Scales and fissures on the lower lip with sparing of the surrounding skin
key_facts: Female patient in her early 40s
No other medical history
Topical corticosteroids ineffective in controlling symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, crusts, and excoriations
Scales and fissures on the lower lip
Normal blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement
Normal urine porphyrin analysis
Skin biopsy showed spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis
Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis
CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells in the germinal center
Phototest with solar simulator showed delayed erythema to UV-A

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate and CD20 negative cells

shortlist.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate and CD20 positive cells

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Germinal center formation and CD20 positive cells

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic pruritic skin condition with erythematous papules

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate and atypical lymphocytes

shortlist.label: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic pruritic skin condition with erythematous papules and scales

shortlist.label: Cutaneous marginal zone lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate and lymphoid follicles

shortlist.label: Sézary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic pruritic skin condition with erythematous papules and lymphadenopathy

raw.rationale: The presence of a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center, along with CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells, is characteristic of primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The presence of CD20 positive cells suggests a B-cell origin, which is not typical for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathological features do not match those of mycosis fungoides, which typically shows epidermotropism and atypical lymphocytes

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: The lack of atypical lymphocytes and the presence of a nodular infiltrate with germinal centers are not characteristic of lymphomatoid papulosis

rejected.label: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica
rejected.why: The clinical and histological features do not match those of pityriasis lichenoides chronica, which typically shows a more superficial infiltrate and lack of germinal centers

rejected.label: Cutaneous marginal zone lymphoma
rejected.why: The presence of a nodular infiltrate with germinal centers and CD20 positive cells is more characteristic of primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma

rejected.label: Sézary syndrome
rejected.why: The lack of systemic symptoms and the presence of a localized skin infiltrate are not characteristic of Sézary syndrome

rejected.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While the presence of CD20 positive cells suggests a B-cell origin, the specific diagnosis of primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma is more precise based on the clinical and histological features
